newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court sentences 41 students over campus unrest.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court sentences 41 students over campus unrest.

text.p: A South Korean court sentenced 15 students to jail on Friday and gave suspended terms to another 26 for their part in violent pro-North Korean protests on a Seoul campus in August, court officials said.
Six of the jailed students were convicted under national security laws that ban all unauthorised contact with communist North Korea.
Jail terms were set at between eight months and 2-1/2 years, the officials said. All the suspended sentences were for two years.

It was the second mass sentencing of radical students this week on charges connected with the unrest at Seoul's prestigious Yonsei University. On Tuesday, 51 students were jailed for up to three years and another 59 given suspended prison terms.
A total of 444 students, many of them members of a leftist student council, the Hanchongryon, have been charged.
